text:
incident-bot: PAGER: Runtime latency spike on canary-rl1 after rollforward. p95 > 1200ms, error rate x3. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/r/abc123

maria-nguyen: seeing it now, started ~21:09 UTC. Rollforward v2.3.4 went to canary-rl1 at 21:07.

deploy-bot: Deploy v2.3.4 rollforward -> canary-rl1 completed at 21:07:14 UTC. No manual pauses.

jess-sre: kernel_selector falling back to generic path repeatedly on canary hosts, likely due to queue/backpressure. Snippet: ```
[21:09:35] kernel_selector: fallback_triggered reason=queue_growth->latency_budget_exceeded
[21:09:36] kernel_selector: switched_to=generic_path
```

raj-patel: I'm oncall. what's customer impact?

anna-cs: CS: 3 paying customers reported request timeouts in the last 10m, two tickets open with severity=P2.

maria-nguyen: attempting rapid mitigation: toggling adaptive-batching FF on canary first to avoid full rollback. Running: `/ff disable adaptive-batching --env=canary-rl1`

ev an-ops: queue lengths jumped, batch windows widened => much larger microbatches, KV cache thrash. Disabling batching should reduce batch size but kernel fallback may persist until queues drain.

raj-patel: agree. Maria, flip FF, I'll prepare kernel affinity override if needed.

deploy-bot: Feature flag `adaptive-batching` disabled on canary-rl1 by maria-nguyen (OK). Changes taking effect.

jess-sre: after FF off p95 dropped from ~1200ms -> ~420ms, error rate down but still some kernel fallback traces. Logs show prefetch/eviction spikes.

maria-nguyen: starting rollback to v2.3.3 as contingency — rollback initiated, ETA ~3m.

deploy-bot: Rollback v2.3.4 -> v2.3.3 started for canary-rl1. Running rollback hooks.

incident-bot: ESCALATION: Pager threshold still hit; paging ENG-SRE lead for verification.

raj-patel: handing off to jess-sre for post-rollback verification and stabilization.

jess-sre: rollback completed at 21:13:58 UTC. Canary now on v2.3.3. p95 trending ~240ms and steady. No kernel_selector fallback logs in last 2m. KV cache hit ratio recovering.

anna-cs: will tell affected customers: rollback mitigated impact, incident under investigation.

maria-nguyen: short summary for postmortem: rollforward included a batching window heuristic change that increased microbatch sizes under our canary load pattern -> queue growth -> kernel selector fallback to generic path -> p95 spike + errors. Mitigations performed: disabled FF, then rolled back. Next actions: revert heuristic, add canary load simulation during PR gating, add automated quick-rollback on canary failure, improve kernel_selector telemetry.

jess-sre: creating incident ticket and tagging serving/runtime/release teams. Assigning follow-ups: root-cause, test harness, and rollback runbook updates.

raj-patel: closing handoff — monitor for 30m then de-escalate if stable. :thumbsup:
